learningObjective: Distinguish SPMD-style compiler-driven parallelization (as in GSPMD) from manual multi-controller / MPMD approaches.
stem: Consider GSPMD-style SPMD partitioning versus manual/MPMD-style parallelization for a large model. Which THREE of the following statements are correct?

options.text: SPMD forbids per-rank differences of any kind; if any operator would have to execute differently on different ranks, the program cannot be expressed in SPMD and must fall back to MPMD.

Manual / MPMD-style parallelism generally requires the user to author per-rank code paths and to explicitly place ops and issue collectives, which is more expressive but more error-prone than SPMD annotations.

SPMD partitioning transforms a single-device-semantics program into a single per-rank program in which each op has been rewritten according to sharding annotations, and reshard boundaries are compiled into explicit collectives.
GSPMD relies on sharding annotations that the user places on some tensors/ops; the partitioner then propagates these annotations to the rest of the graph.

explanation: A, B, D reflect the GSPMD design: (A) one SPMD program per rank, generated by a partitioner that inserts collectives at reshard boundaries; (B) user-provided annotations propagated by the compiler; (D) manual approaches trade expressive freedom for more per-rank code complexity. C is false: SPMD permits per-rank parameterization (rank id, shard offsets, even control-flow specialization) — 'single program' does not mean 'identical execution on every rank'.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: SPMD allows per-rank differences via rank-id-dependent computation.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: MPMD is more expressive but more manual.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: standard SPMD partitioning transforms operators and inserts collectives.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: annotations are user hints; propagation is compiler responsibility.

assumptions: The compiler is at least as expressive as XLA/HLO with sharding attributes.
Users understand that annotations are hints, not exhaustive specifications.
nonImplications: Does not imply that SPMD is universally faster than MPMD; certain asymmetric patterns can be more natural in MPMD.
Does not imply that annotations alone determine performance; the partitioner's cost model matters.

sourceRefs.locator: §1–§3 SPMD design and comparison with manual approaches
